checks.what: Commonwealth of England loses Ireland to the Kingdom of Ireland, May 1660. The page says 'The kingdom's order was restored 1660 with the restoration of Charles II', 'England, Scotland and Ireland were ruled as a republic until 1660', and the infobox gives 'Dependency of England (1542-1707)'. The page gives no month. May matches the commonwealth-of-england dossier's own sourced end (ledger/16, May 1660). The region resolves to 347 cells: the 344 cells of 'Ireland (island)' plus 3 coastal cells in Clew Bay, Galway Bay and Dundalk Bay, all on the Irish coast, nothing off the island. Trial p1660: the commonwealth/kingdom-of-ireland conflict (64 cell-years) and the kingdom-of-england_1662 snap that removed 279 cells are both gone. All 347 cells are kingdom-of-ireland, vassal of England, at the ends of 1660 and 1662 and on 1 Jan 1670 and 1 Jan 1680. The 344 are contested from 1689 (dossier ledger/15) and back in the vassal tint at 1 Jan 1700 (trial p1690). The published 1700 anchor had 3 nobody cells and 2 England cells there.

Kingdom of Ireland gains the island from Kingdom of England, June 1660. Same page support and same region as events/3. In trial p1660 it moves the 2 coastal cells that were nobody's (shown as None -> kingdom-of-ireland, vassal). Without it they would stay outside the kingdom.

Kingdom of Ireland gains the island from nobody, June 1660. Same page and region. It moves no cell in trial p1660 because events/3 and events/4 already cover every cell. It is a harmless safety net, and p1690-p1699 events/0 is likewise a no-op now.

Sweden gains its present-day land from Denmark-Norway, January 1660. The Bromsebro page says Denmark-Norway 'ceded the Norwegian provinces of Jamtland and Harjedalen' and that Idre and Sarna 'were conquered by Dalecarlian peasants', recognised only in 1751. The Denmark-Norway page says the 1660 Copenhagen treaty 'gave Trondelag and Bornholm back' and nothing else, so present Sweden was all Swedish in 1660. The region is country Sweden (2440 cells), but a gain moves only Danish-Norwegian cells. In the trial it moved 1 cell, Idre at 61.69 N 12.22 E. Norway's cells are unchanged against the published 1670 anchor.

Ruling for Sweden over Denmark-Norway inside present Sweden, 1660-1669. It continues p1650-p1659 rulings/0 and has the same page support as events/6. Trial: it settled 5 cell-years in 1660 and 1662 at 63.18 N 12.17 E, 64.54 N 13.83 E and Idre. The other 66 cell-years of the pair, in Trondelag and Norway, still go to Denmark-Norway, as Copenhagen 1660 requires.

swedish-empire_1662 override. It keeps the dossier's own correction (the Cliopatria 1662 shape without Ghana) and adds the intersect of Sweden with Cliopatria's Denmark-Norway 1662 shape. That intersect resolves to exactly 3 cells: 63.18 N 12.17 E, 64.54 N 13.83 E and 61.69 N 12.22 E, all Jamtland, Harjedalen or Idre-Sarna border cells. No other window overrides this shape. Trial: all 3 stay Swedish 1660-1669, 2432 of Sweden's 2440 cells are Swedish at 1 Jan 1670, and the 8 nobody cells there are not this entry's.

New keyframe united-states-of-america_1791b, 1791-1821. The page quotes Article 2: the line runs from the Lake of the Woods 'on a due west course to the river Mississippi', then 'along the middle of the said river' to 31 N, and 'the Mississippi does not extend that far northward'. That puts Minnesota east of the river, Wisconsin and Kentucky in the United States. The Minnesota part resolves to 289 cells, east of the river and of the meridian through the river's source. Trial p1790: the US 1791 snap now removes 36 cells instead of 394, the spanish-empire_1792 snap of 295 cells is gone, and at 1 Jan 1800 Minnesota east of the river (289), Wisconsin (636) and Kentucky (442) are wholly US. Trials p1800, p1810 and p1820: Wisconsin and Kentucky stay whole through 1830 with no flicker at 1821/22. Minnesota is all US at 1 Jan 1820 and 1 Jan 1830; 4 cells go to british-colonial-empire in 1822-1823, already known and not caused by this entry. Residuals are listed under problems: 8 east-bank cells near St. Cloud and Little Falls, inherited from the p1780-p1789 polygon, and southern Georgia, left out on purpose. The 1805 snap now removes 1390 western cells instead of 453; that comes from the US dossier edit of 23:49, not from this union, which can only add cells to the keyframe.

Ruling for Rupert's Land over Upper Canada on the 49-50.3 N band of Ontario, 1791-1841. The Province of Quebec page says the Quebec Act took Quebec 'north to the southern boundary of lands owned by the Hudson's Bay Company, or Rupert's Land' and that the 1791 Act 'divided the colony in two at the Ottawa River'. The Upper Canada page says the Act 'did not yet specify official borders' and names no northern boundary or change of it up to 10 February 1841, so keeping the status quo of p1780-p1789 rulings/1 is the right reading. The region resolves to 477 Ontario cells. At 1 Jan 1800, 400 are Rupert's Land, 76 Upper Canada and 1 nobody. Trials: 532 cell-years settled in 1791 and 798 in 1812, 1813 and 1815. No flip in the 1810s and no Upper Canada/Rupert's Land conflict left in the 1820s.

Ruling for the United States over british-empire (Cliopatria 'British Empire', the East India Company dossier) in Minnesota, 1791-1809. The page names no Company holding in North America: the Company 'gained control of large parts of the Indian subcontinent and Saint Helena'. The Treaty of Paris page puts the land east of the Mississippi up to the Lake of the Woods line in the United States. The region is all of Minnesota, wider than the 'stray cell' the why names, but in the trials it acted only on US treaty land: the Arrowhead cells at 48.03 N 90.22 W and 47.99 N 90.45 W (1791-1800) and 4 Mille Lacs cells east of the river at 46.2-46.5 N 93.1-93.4 W (1805-1807). It never touched the Red River cells, which Rupert's Land holds.

Ruling for Rupert's Land over French Louisiana in Minnesota north of 47 N less the Leech Lake pocket, 1800-1804. The page says 'The eastern boundary of the Louisiana purchase was the Mississippi River, from its source', that the purchase covered only 'the portion of Minnesota west of the Mississippi River' and ran 'to Rupert's Land in the north', and that land north of 49 N 'was ceded to the UK in exchange for parts of the Red River Basin south of 49th parallel' in the Treaty of 1818. So the Red River basin was not Louisiana's. The region resolves to 315 cells; at 1 Jan 1800, 110 are Rupert's Land (the Red River valley west of the Mississippi's source) and 205 are US. Trial: 440 cell-years settled. The 23 Minnesota cells French Louisiana still takes from Rupert's Land are exactly the Leech Lake pocket (47.0-47.46 N, 95.2-93.5 W), which lies inside the river's upper loop and drains to the Mississippi, so leaving it to Louisiana is right. Rupert's Land keeps the 110 cells at 1 Jan 1810.

problems: Not caused by these entries; this needs a dossier or gazetteer fix. One land cell of Achill Island (85182343fffffff, 53.94 N 10.11 W) is in neither the gazetteer's 'Ireland (island)' region nor country Ireland or Mayo, so it is nobody's in every year (published 1660 and 1670 anchors and all trials). Fix: add it to kingdom-of-ireland_1660's correction, or to the gazetteer's Ireland region.

Residual next to p1790-p1799 keyframe_overrides/1. 8 cells east of the Mississippi between Elk River and Little Falls are Spanish Empire land 1783-1799, in the published 1790 anchor and in the trial: 45.40 N 93.63 W, 45.51 N 93.80 W, 45.61 N 93.97 W, 45.72 N 94.14 W, 45.76 N 93.93 W, 45.87 N 94.10 W, 45.97 N 94.27 W, 46.13 N 94.23 W. Cause: the Minnesota polygon that p1780-p1789 keyframe_overrides/0-1 and 1791b share cuts a diagonal from 95.2 W 47.2 N to 93.2 W 45.0 N, which runs east of the river. A fix needs a matching change in p1780-p1789 and p1790-p1799, done together so 1790/1791 does not flicker. Widen the polygon's south-west corner, for example points 95.2 W 47.2 N, 94.7 W 46.4 N, 94.7 W 45.5 N, 93.8 W 45.0 N, and let the existing 'west of the river' minus cut along the river. French Louisiana takes these cells in 1800 and the US in 1804.

Left on purpose by keyframe_overrides/1 (pages silent). 35 southern Georgia cells south of 31 N, which p1780-p1789 keyframe_overrides/0-1 give the US for 1783-1790, fall to nobody from 1791 as in the published draft. The Treaty of Paris page as served quotes only the 31st-parallel part of Article 2, not the St. Marys line. A later seam pass should open a page that gives Georgia's 1783/1795 southern boundary (e.g. Pinckney's Treaty) and extend 1791b, or else withdraw the 1783-1790 cells.

Outside p1800-p1809 rulings/2's region. French Louisiana still takes 291 Rupert's Land cells of the North Dakota Red River basin in 1800, by the size rule. These are the cells p1760-p1769 rulings/0 gives Rupert's Land. The same Louisiana Purchase page puts the Red River basin outside the purchase until 1818, so a ruling for Rupert's Land on North Dakota's Red River valley for 1800-1804 would be the matching repair. The US then inherits these cells in 1804 and drops them to nobody in 1805.

Not caused by sm-05. The US 1805 snap now releases 1390 cells of the western plains and Rockies to nobody (published draft: 453), and the US 1820 snap adds 661. Both follow the united-states-of-america dossier edit of 2 Nov 23:49 (ledger/24 and the 1805 correction 'Less the overshoot of the Louisiana region'), made after the published draft of 22:32.
